distractors.reason: We don't say 'deeply cheap'. 'Deeply' is used with feelings or emotions, like 'deeply concerned'.
We don't say 'fully cheap'. 'Fully' means completely and is used with words like 'fully aware' or 'fully booked'.
We don't say 'highly cheap'. 'Highly' is used with positive or formal qualities, like 'highly recommended'.

example_sentence: These shoes are ___ cheap, so I will buy two pairs.
l1_interference: Polscy uczniowie mogą wybierać 'deeply' albo 'highly', bo po polsku 'bardzo' ma wiele odpowiedników. Przy przymiotniku 'cheap' w angielskim używamy zawsze 'very'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the most common degree adverb before everyday adjectives such as cheap, expensive or good. Other degree adverbs are limited to specific adjectives.

related_collocations.example: The new shop has totally different prices.
The offer on these bags is really good.

memory_tip: VERY + everyday adjectives (very cheap, very expensive) | DEEPLY + feelings (deeply concerned) | FULLY + completion (fully aware) | HIGHLY + praise (highly recommended)
